### More menu skips keyboard focus **Medium Severity** Opening the overflow menu never moves focus into the list. `selectedId` is `null`, so the focus-the-selected-option path does not run, and Arrow/Enter on the trigger only call `setIsOpen(true)`. Keyboard users cannot walk the overflowed categories, which is how most filters are reached at popup width.
Additional Locations (1) - [`ui/components/app/perps/perps-market-categories/perps-category-rail.tsx#L184-L188`](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-extension/blob/40ec37067a684add7b4673bc7da2041e94e803a0/ui/components/app/perps/perps-market-categories/perps-category-rail.tsx#L184-L188)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 40ec37067a684add7b4673bc7da2041e94e803a0. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Stuck New filter cannot return to All **Medium Severity** A `?filter=new` link (or a New pill that later disappears) still applies the `new` filter, but `new` is omitted from the rail when there are no uncategorized markets. The rail no longer has an `All` pill, and `onClear` only exists on the active pill, so there is no control that returns the list to every market. Watchlist already falls back to `all` when hidden; `new` does not.
Additional Locations (1) - [`ui/pages/perps/market-list/index.tsx#L613-L624`](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-extension/blob/d76f1431b50ffa1d73c805c0d7bc0debc1038e81/ui/pages/perps/market-list/index.tsx#L613-L624)
 
Triggered by learned rule: Perps formatters and hooks mirror mobile — do not flag intentional parity patterns Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit d76f1431b50ffa1d73c805c0d7bc0debc1038e81. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

Fixed in a5d94a0 — good catch, this was reachable.

A category now stays on the rail while it is the active filter even when the live data no longer offers it, so `?filter=new` with no uncategorized markets renders a pressed `New` pill, and pressing it clears back to every market. Watchlist is excluded from that fallback since it is the header star's state, not a rail slot.

Regression test: `keeps a pill for an active category the data no longer offers` in `ui/pages/perps/market-list/index.test.tsx`.

Resolved in a5d94a0 by removal. The overflow menu is gone — the rail now wraps, so every category pill is on screen and Tab-reachable, and the `Dropdown` props that existed only for that menu (`triggerLabel`, `triggerClassName`, `triggerAriaLabel`, `menuClassName`, nullable `selectedId`, the focus-first-option-on-open branch) are reverted. `dropdown.tsx` is back to its pre-PR behaviour; only its path moved.

Guard for the property this thread was about: `reaches every pill from the keyboard` in `perps-category-rail.test.tsx`.

body:
Non-blocking: this reserves Products height, but the loaded tree puts `PerpsWatchlist` above Products and this skeleton does not.

If the user has a watchlist, that block appears after load and the chips jump down. Mirror Watchlist in this loading tree (or a matching-height placeholder) so the slot stays stable.

Stale: the overflow rail no longer promotes the active category into the visible row. `selectedId` is set for overflowed filters and `isTriggerActive` paints the More trigger.

Please update this comment so the next reader does not “fix” that path back to promotion.

The cached widths are only invalidated when `keysSignature` changes, but a pill's width also changes when it becomes the active one: `PerpsMarketCategoryPill` renders the `CircleX` clear glyph (plus its gap) only while `isActive`. Selecting a category that is currently the last one that fits therefore widens it without a remeasure, and since the row is `overflow-x-clip` the clear control — the only way back to the unfiltered list from the rail — can end up clipped off the right edge. The same applies to the `More` trigger, which grows when it takes the `More, <category> selected` label.

Suggest folding the active category into the signature (or remeasuring on selection change) so the fit is recomputed with the widths actually rendered.

`useLayoutEffect` with no dependency array runs `measure()` after every render. The market list re-renders on every live market tick, so this does a synchronous layout read (`clientWidth`/`offsetWidth`) on each one, and the `ResizeObserver` below already covers the case this is guarding against (the row's own size changing).

A dependency list of `[measure]` plus the observer should cover mount, category changes and resizes without the per-tick reads.

body:
The comment says the skeleton reserves the Products section's height "in the same slot it occupies once loaded", but the two trees do not line up. In the loaded tree the order is `PerpsWatchlist` -> `PerpsProducts` -> `PerpsTopMovers`, while here Products follows two `PerpsSectionSkeleton`s with no slot standing in for the watchlist. `PerpsWatchlist` returns `null` when the list is empty, so for a user who has starred markets the watchlist section appears above Products on load and pushes it down — the jump the skeleton is meant to prevent.

Related: on line 503 `isLoading={marketsLoading}` can never be `true`, because the early return above already requires `marketsLoading === false` (it is part of `isLoading`). Worth simplifying so the prop does not read as a live state.

`useCategoryRailOverflow` is called unconditionally, so the `Wrap` layout (the Products section) mounts the measuring hook as well even though it never attaches `rowRef` and never uses `visibleCount`. That is a `ResizeObserver` plus a layout effect per render on the Perps tab for a layout that by design never overflows.

Also worth noting for `Overflow` on line 133: until the first measurement lands, `visibleCount` is `null` and every pill renders, so at popup width there is a frame with all categories laid out before they collapse into `More`. A first-paint hidden/invisible measuring pass would avoid the flash.

When the watchlist filter is active this passes `'watchlist'` into the rail as `selectedCategory`. No pill matches it, so nothing is marked `aria-pressed` on the rail (correct outcome), but the rail still treats itself as holding a selection — `overflowSelection` is computed against it and `handleOverflowChange` compares against it, so a category can never be cleared through the `More` menu while the watchlist is on.

Since watchlist state lives on the header star, passing `null` for it (same as `'all'`) makes the rail's contract "category or nothing" and removes the special case.

`"$1 markets"` renders as "1 markets" when the filter leaves a single market — reachable today with a narrow category or a search-adjacent filter. Worth a singular/plural pair (or dropping the noun) so the count line never reads ungrammatically.

Separate note on this file: the `ETF` -> `ETFs` and `Index` -> `Indices` rewordings land in `en`/`en_GB` only, so the other locales keep the singular until Crowdin catches up. Fine if that is the expected flow, just worth flagging if the copy is meant to ship translated.

This doc says the category rail's overflow menu "never" holds a selection "because the active category is promoted into the visible row instead", but the final behaviour is the opposite: the rail splits in source order, the active category can land in the menu, and `PerpsCategoryRail` passes `selectedId={overflowSelection}` with `isTriggerActive` exactly for that case. Reads as leftover from the earlier promote-the-active-pill approach and would mislead the next change to this prop.

"the market-list filter dropdown and the Perps tab category pills" — the filter dropdown is removed in this PR (`filter-select` is deleted). The consumers now are the market list's category rail and the Products chips, both via `PerpsMarketCategoryPill`, plus the `More` menu's option labels.
